Pass.description: No demonstrable flaw stands anywhere in the reviewed steps: the step under review and every earlier one hold as written, and every previously recorded objection is resolved. Pass judges correctness and support only — never whether some extra point might enrich what comes later. Use verdict "Pass", set step to the current review position, a substantive one-or-two-sentence reason naming the check you actually made (at least 30 characters — never placeholder text), an empty suggestion, and the fixed evidence object with kind "none" and every detail field empty.

Build.description: One reviewed step is sound as far as it goes but has a NECESSARY gap in its own support: a missing justification, an unstated assumption doing real work, or an uncovered case its claim depends on. Build ONLY when the chain cannot stand without the addition — an enhancement that is merely nice to have is a Pass, not a Build. Use verdict "Build", set step to the gapped step (the current one or any earlier one), a substantive reason (at least 30 characters), the concrete non-empty suggestion (at least 20 characters), and the fixed evidence object with kind "none" and every detail field empty.

Interrupt.description: A DEMONSTRATED flaw stands in one of the reviewed steps — the current one or any earlier one — such that the chain is wrong at or after it. Interrupt requires evidence: runnable script, self-contained math derivation, or real reference. A suspicion is not an Interrupt: verify it with your capabilities first, and if verification does not substantiate it, it is not a flaw. Use verdict "Interrupt", set step to the flawed step, the specific substantive reason (at least 30 characters), and the evidence object; leave the suggestion empty unless you have a concrete repair to hand the thinker.
